items.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: Tatum of course is all our Gods... I have about six Tatum CDs that I have on all the time... you find chord changes he makes that you wouldn’t think of... he knows a lot more than I do.

ctx.x: That was my main goal in life. And I made it, in about 1950 I got into my first studio thing and I stayed in the studios for about 20 years. But he was very smart, he let me play 45 minutes of all the technical stuff, the Hanon and Czerny and all this and the Bach and Mozart, it was mostly technical stuff. He never pushed me into learning by rote or either way, the Rachmaninoff and the heavy stuff that you have to spend weeks and weeks and weeks before you can play the thing. And he just worked on my facility and…
Amazing. The Tatum books, had someone transcribed the music? When you say you were reading Tatum books.
